lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Month one of your first job in the city. It is 9:02 am. Your phone buzzes.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Salary credited?! It's real. I am officially a person with money.

lines.speaker: kabir
lines.text: {name}! FLATMATE! I heard the buzz. Biryani tonight? New sneakers? A tiny trip to Goa?

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Kabir, it has been in my account for forty seconds.

lines.speaker: kabir
lines.text: And it is already lonely. Money wants to be spent. It's science.

lines.speaker: asha
lines.text: Congratulations, {name}! First salary is a big day. Enjoy some of it, really.

lines.speaker: asha
lines.text: But before it all vanishes, come for chai on Sunday. I'll tell you what I wish someone had told me.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Sunday. Asha's balcony. Two cups of chai and a plate of samosas.

lines.speaker: asha
lines.text: When I started working, a samosa at my office canteen cost ₹10. Guess what it costs now?

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Twelve?

lines.speaker: asha
lines.text: Twenty. Same samosa. Same potato. That slow price rise is called inflation.

lines.speaker: kabir
lines.text: So the samosa got richer and I got poorer? Rude.

lines.speaker: asha
lines.text: Exactly. Money sitting idle quietly buys less every year. It's a silent thief, no mask, no noise.

lines.speaker: asha
lines.text: Saving keeps money safe. Investing gives it a chance to keep up with that thief over time. Both have a job.

nodes.title: Outrun the price rise
nodes.intro: Prices are chasing your rupees. Run 150 metres and dodge the dips!

lines.speaker: kabir
lines.text: Forget samosas. My cousin's friend's gym trainer has a HOT TIP. Guaranteed to double. Super secret.

lines.speaker: asha
lines.text: If it's a secret, why does your gym trainer know it?

lines.speaker: kabir
lines.text: ...He's very well connected?

lines.speaker: asha
lines.text: Nobody can guarantee doubling. Anyone who promises that is selling something, usually to you.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Then how do regular people invest without being experts?

lines.speaker: asha
lines.text: One common way is a mutual fund. Lots of people pool their money, and a professional team invests it as per a stated plan.

lines.speaker: kabir
lines.text: A group trip, but for money. I'm in. Who's driving?

question.explanation: Paying your future self first, then enjoying the rest guilt-free, is a habit many patient investors swear by. The amounts are up to you.

payload.prompt: Friday night. Kabir is holding two concert tickets and a very hopeful face. What do you do with this month's salary?

options.text: Spend it all. YOLO. Next month is next month's problem.
options.outcome: Great concert! By the 20th you are eating plain rice and calling it 'minimalism'.

options.text: Set aside a slice for goals first, then enjoy the rest.
options.outcome: You go to the concert AND your goals fund grows. Asha sends a thumbs up emoji. A rare honour.

options.text: Put everything into the gym trainer's secret tip.
options.outcome: The trainer stops replying. Kabir says the tip 'is in a consolidation phase'. Hmm.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Okay. Plan: needs first, a slice for the future, then fun. Written on a napkin, so it's official.

lines.speaker: asha
lines.text: That napkin is worth more than any hot tip. Next week, I'll take you both to the zoo.

lines.speaker: kabir
lines.text: An actual zoo? With animals?

lines.speaker: asha
lines.text: A Fund Zoo. You'll see.

chapters.title: The Fund Zoo
chapters.subtitle: NAV, fund managers, wild fund types

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Saturday morning. Asha hands you each an imaginary ticket. 'The Fund Zoo', it says.

lines.speaker: kabir
lines.text: I opened an investing app and it keeps saying 'NAV'. I nodded like I knew. I did not know.

lines.speaker: asha
lines.text: NAV is the price of one unit of a fund. When you invest, you buy units at that day's NAV.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: So a lower NAV means a cheaper, better fund?

lines.speaker: asha
lines.text: Nope! A low NAV isn't a bargain and a high one isn't expensive. It just tells you the value per unit.

lines.speaker: asha
lines.text: Every animal here has a keeper. In a fund, that's the fund manager and their team.

lines.speaker: kabir
lines.text: Do they work for free? Out of love for animals?

lines.speaker: asha
lines.text: Sadly no. Funds charge a yearly fee called the expense ratio. Think of it as the zoo's entry ticket, paid a little every day.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: So I should check the ticket price, not just how cute the animals look.

lines.speaker: asha
lines.text: Exactly. Small fees add up over many years, so it's worth reading the label.

nodes.title: Merge into units
nodes.intro: Small coins merge into bigger ones, like small amounts pooling into a fund. Reach 200!

lines.speaker: asha
lines.text: Now the fun part. Meet the residents. That cheetah? An equity fund. Fast, exciting, and very moody.

lines.speaker: kabir
lines.text: Cheetah. Mine. Done. Fastest wins.

lines.speaker: asha
lines.text: It also has bad days when it just lies in the sun and sulks. Equity can swing a lot in the short term.

lines.speaker: asha
lines.text: The tortoise is a debt fund. Slower, steadier, not zero risk, but calmer.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: And the zebra? Black and white stripes?

lines.speaker: asha
lines.text: A hybrid fund, a bit of both. And that elephant just follows the herd. That's an index fund: it simply tracks a market index.

question.explanation: There's no single best animal. Match the fund's temperament to how soon you need the money and how much swing you can sit through.

payload.prompt: Kabir wants money for a bike in 6 months. He points at the fund with the best return last year. What do you tell him?

options.text: Last year's champion! Can't go wrong.
options.outcome: Asha: 'Last year's results don't promise next year's. Cheetahs have off seasons too.'

options.text: First think about when you need it and how much ups and downs you can handle.
options.outcome: Kabir: 'Six months... a moody cheetah might be sulking right when I need my bike.' Growth!

options.text: Pick the one with the coolest animal name.
options.outcome: Kabir chooses 'Turbo Panther'. It isn't a real fund. It's his gaming username.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: I want to invest, but I don't have a giant pile of money. Do I wait until I'm rich?

lines.speaker: asha
lines.text: Waiting to be rich before investing is like waiting to be fit before joining a gym.

lines.speaker: asha
lines.text: A SIP lets you invest a fixed amount every month, even a small one. The habit matters more than the size at the start.

lines.speaker: kabir
lines.text: Like my gym membership! Except I would actually use it.

lines.speaker: asha
lines.text: Especially that. A SIP shows up every month, even when you don't feel like it.

lines.speaker: asha
lines.text: Here's a neat side effect. Same amount each month: when the NAV is low, you get more units. When it's high, fewer.

lines.speaker: kabir
lines.text: So when prices drop, it's basically a sale? I LOVE a sale.

lines.speaker: asha
lines.text: That's rupee cost averaging. It doesn't guarantee a profit, but it means you don't have to guess the perfect day.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Good, because my track record of guessing things is mostly about cricket. And it's bad.

nodes.title: Stack your SIPs
nodes.intro: One block a month, every month. Stack 8 blocks and keep the tower steady!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Eight months later. Every headline is red. Kabir bursts through the door.

lines.speaker: kabir
lines.text: ABORT! ABORT! The market fell! My app is red! My SOUL is red!

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Mine is down too. My stomach just did a little backflip.

lines.speaker: asha
lines.text: Breathe, both of you. Dips are a normal part of investing. I've lived through several.

lines.speaker: asha
lines.text: The question isn't 'is it red today?'. It's 'has my goal or timeline changed?'

question.explanation: Markets go up and down. If your goal is years away and your plan still fits, staying the course is often wiser than reacting to one scary month.

payload.prompt: Your long-term investments are down 15% this month (illustrative). Your goal is 10 years away. Kabir is hovering over the 'Sell all' button. What do you do?

options.text: Stop the SIP and sell everything before it gets worse.
options.outcome: You lock in the fall, and your SIP habit stops too. If prices bounce back later, you're watching from outside. Kabir quietly uninstalls the app.

options.text: Stay the course: keep the SIP going and check the goal still fits.
options.outcome: Your monthly SIP keeps buying units during the dip. Asha raises her chai cup in salute.

options.text: Borrow money to invest more, the dip is a sure thing!
options.outcome: Nothing about the market is a sure thing, and borrowed money is stressful. Kabir now owes his sister ₹5,000.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One year after that first salary. Same balcony. Same samosas. Slightly more expensive.

lines.speaker: kabir
lines.text: I have news. I did NOT sell during the dip. I didn't follow a single hot tip. I'm a changed man.

lines.speaker: asha
lines.text: Proud of you, Kabir. And you, {name}, you kept your SIP going through the scary month.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Turns out the secret was boring: start small, stay steady, keep learning.

lines.speaker: asha
lines.text: Boring is underrated. Now enjoy that samosa. You've earned it.
